findings.control_name: No CloudWatch Alarm for Secrets Manager PutSecretValue
findings.control_description: No CloudWatch alarm monitors CloudTrail for PutSecretValue API calls. ACM does not auto-renew imported certificates — the owner must replace them manually before expiry. Without Config recording, there is no configuration change timeline to detect when the certificate entered the near-expiry window and no Config rule to alert on the approaching deadline. The combination means an expiring certificate with no automated detection — the first signal is a production TLS handshake failure. Either control alone mitigates: replacing the certificate before expiry prevents the outage; enabling Config detects the expiring certificate and can trigger a notification or remediation workflow.

ACM ACME endpoint allows wildcard certificate issuance AND CloudTrail is not enabled. A wildcard certificate (*.example.com) covers every subdomain — one compromised private key or one leaked certificate enables impersonation of any service under the domain. The combination is unrestricted wildcard cert issuance with invisible certificate operations. Either control alone mitigates: disabling wildcard issuance limits certificates to specific subdomains; enabling CloudTrail records all certificate issuance for detection and forensics.

ElastiCache cluster security group allows broad ingress (0.0.0.0/0 on cache ports) AND CloudTrail is not enabled. Broad ingress means any host with network connectivity can reach the cache endpoint. Without CloudTrail, API calls that modify the cluster configuration (ModifyReplicationGroup, CreateSnapshot, DeleteCacheCluster) leave no audit record. The combination is a wide-open cache endpoint with invisible control-plane activity — an attacker can snapshot the cluster for offline data extraction and the API call is never logged. Either control alone mitigates: restricting the security group limits who can reach the endpoint; enabling CloudTrail records configuration changes for detection and forensics.

Redis cache has no AUTH token AND the VPC has no flow logs. Without AUTH, any client with network access reads and writes cached data (sessions, credentials, application state). Without flow logs, there is no record of which hosts connected to the cache endpoint. The combination is an unauthenticated data store with zero network forensics — an attacker exfiltrates cached data and the breach leaves no evidence trail. Either control alone mitigates: AUTH blocks unauthorized access; flow logs record connection attempts for post-incident investigation.

ElastiCache cluster has no at-rest encryption AND AWS Config is not recording. Without at-rest encryption, cached data (sessions, credentials, PII) is stored in plaintext on the cluster nodes and in any snapshots. Without Config recording, the encryption posture of the cluster is not tracked — there is no Config rule to flag the missing encryption and no configuration timeline to detect when encryption was disabled or never enabled. The combination means plaintext data at rest with no compliance visibility into the misconfiguration. Either control alone mitigates: enabling encryption protects the data; enabling Config detects the missing encryption and can trigger automated remediation.

fix_plan.action: Enable MFA on the root account using a hardware MFA device or virtual MFA app. Navigate to IAM > Security credentials > MFA.
Delete the root access keys. Create IAM users or roles with least-privilege policies for programmatic access.
Enable the Config recorder with all resource types. Run: aws configservice put-configuration-recorder --configuration-recorder name=default,roleARN=arn:...,recordingGroup={allSupported=true}
Deploy Config Rules for your compliance requirements. Start with AWS managed rules for common checks (encrypted-volumes, restricted-common-ports, etc).

Add a Secrets Manager data-event selector to a CloudTrail trail covering the account or the relevant secret ARNs: aws cloudtrail put-event-selectors --trail-name <trail> --advanced-event-selectors '[{"Name":"Secrets Manager data events","FieldSelectors": [{"Field":"eventCategory","Equals":["Data"]}, {"Field":"resources.type","Equals":["AWS::SecretsManager::Secret"]}]}]'. For high-volume environments, restrict the resource ARN selector to security-sensitive secrets to bound log-volume cost. Verify the trail's S3 destination has appropriate access controls and retention.

Create a CloudTrail metric filter on eventName = PutSecretValue. To reduce noise from rotation-initiated calls, exclude events where userIdentity.arn matches a known rotation Lambda pattern: '{ $.eventName = "PutSecretValue" && $.userIdentity.arn != "*lambda*rotation*" }'. Wire to a CloudWatch alarm with threshold >= 1 over a 5-minute period. Route to ops on-call so manual modifications surface immediately and trigger investigation.
Configure automatic rotation with a Lambda function. Run: aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id xxx --rotation-lambda-arn arn:aws:lambda:... --rotation-rules AutomaticallyAfterDays=90
Recreate the secret with a customer-managed KMS key specified. Secrets Manager does not allow changing the encryption key after creation.

Either: (a) configure an EventBridge rule on aws.secretsmanager source with detail-type "AWS API Call via CloudTrail" and event names containing rotation failure / lambda invocation errors, then route to a CloudWatch alarm via SNS notification; or (b) create a CloudTrail metric filter on eventName = RotateSecret AND errorCode is present, then a CloudWatch alarm with threshold >= 1 over a 5-minute period. Either path provides minutes-level detection. Verify the alarm action publishes to a topic with at least one confirmed subscriber (see CTL.SNS.LIFECYCLE.UNCONFIRMED.001).
Enable log file validation on the trail. Run: aws cloudtrail update-trail --name xxx --enable-log-file-validation
Update the trail to enable multi-region logging. Run: aws cloudtrail update-trail --name xxx --is-multi-region-trail
Configure the trail to use a KMS key for log encryption. Run: aws cloudtrail update-trail --name xxx --kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:...

Set retention on Cognito-associated log groups to meet the applicable framework's minimum: aws logs put-retention-policy --log-group-name patient-portal --retention-in-days 365 (SOC 2 / PCI-DSS), 2190 (HIPAA), or higher per organizational policy. The catalog already has log-group retention controls (CW-2 LOGGROUP.RETENTION.SHORT) — this control adds Cognito-specific framing when those log groups carry auth events.

Migrate the user pool to an approved region (Cognito does not support cross- region replication; migration requires user re-registration or a custom migration trigger). Add an SCP that denies cognito-idp:CreateUserPool in non-approved regions to prevent future occurrences.

Configure custom_email_sender or KMS- encrypted attributes on the user pool using a customer-managed KMS key. For pools subject to compliance requirements (HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP), CMK encryption is typically a baseline requirement; default AWS-managed encryption may not satisfy auditors.

Add email to auto_verified_attributes on the user pool: aws cognito-idp update-user-pool with --auto-verified-attributes email. After this, signup requires the user to receive and submit a verification code sent to the email — confirming control of the address before the account is usable. Existing users with unverified email need a separate backfill or re-confirmation flow.
Set MfaConfiguration to ON (required) on the user pool. Run: aws cognito-idp set-user-pool-mfa-config --user-pool-id xxx --mfa-configuration ON --software-token-mfa-configuration Enabled=true

Enable advanced security features on the user pool with risk_configuration set so high-risk events block authentication and medium-risk events require step-up authentication: aws cognito-idp set-risk-configuration with appropriate actions on Compromised Credentials and Account Takeover Risk decisions. Advanced security adds adaptive throttling that detects brute-force patterns and locks the offending IP / username combination.
Enable SSE-KMS on the topic. Run: aws sns set-topic-attributes --topic-arn xxx --attribute-name KmsMasterKeyId --attribute-value arn:aws:kms:...
Update the key policy to restrict Principal to specific IAM roles or accounts. Remove any statements with Principal "*".

fix_plan.action: Modify the instance to disable public accessibility. Run: aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier xxx --no-publicly-accessible --apply-immediately
Enable automated backups with at least 7 days retention. Run: aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier xxx --backup-retention-period 7 --apply-immediately
Storage encryption can only be enabled at creation time. Create a snapshot, copy it with encryption enabled, then restore to a new encrypted instance. Enable encryption by default for new instances.

Enable CloudWatch log exports for the database engine. Run: aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier xxx --cloudwatch-logs-export-configuration '{"EnableLogTypes":["audit","error","slowquery"]}'
Modify the instance to enable Multi-AZ. Run: aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier xxx --multi-az --apply-immediately
Update the table encryption to use a customer-managed KMS key. Run: aws dynamodb update-table --table-name xxx --sse-specification Enabled=true,SSEType=KMS,KMSMasterKeyId=arn:...
Enable SSE-KMS on the queue. Run: aws sqs set-queue-attributes --queue-url xxx --attributes KmsMasterKeyId=arn:aws:kms:...
In-transit encryption can only be enabled at cluster creation. Create a new replication group with TransitEncryptionEnabled=true and migrate data from the existing cluster.
Enable VPC flow logs to CloudWatch Logs or S3. Run: aws ec2 create-flow-logs --resource-type VPC --resource-ids vpc-xxx --traffic-type ALL --log-destination-type cloud-watch-logs
